title: parallel has no fail-fast and no per-branch result capture
existing_state: ParallelCommand starts every child step and always waits for all of them to finish via Task.WhenAll (Services/Scripting/Commands/ParallelCommand.cs:40-66); failures are only examined afterwards, in original order, and the first non-suppressed failure becomes the step result identified only as 'Parallel step N failed' (:80-92). ParallelOptions exposes exactly two knobs — Steps and MaxConcurrent (Services/Scripting/Models/ScriptStep.cs:1530-1541). There is no fail_fast to cancel remaining branches when one fails, and no 'into' aggregation: a script cannot ask 'which branches failed?' — results of all branches other than the first failure are discarded.
recommendation: Add two options to ParallelOptions: fail_fast (bool — create a linked CancellationTokenSource and cancel it when a branch returns a non-suppressed failure, so long-running siblings stop instead of burning their full timeouts) and into (capture a list of per-branch records {index, success, message, duration_ms} as a JSON-ish structure the existing table/foreach commands can consume). Both slot cleanly into the existing results collection at :52-55 and the post-WhenAll walk at :80-92. Surface the fields in the Flow Canvas parallel block per Guideline 8.
user_benefit: Fan-out health checks (ping/portcheck/webhook across services) become reportable — 'table: ${parallel_results}' instead of one opaque first-failure message — and a dead branch no longer holds the whole step hostage for its full timeout when fail_fast is on.

evidence.note: all branches always run to completion; ordered post-hoc check returns only the first failure
